findings.title: A disabled addon still draws, outlines and arms drag on every unlocked panel: Unlock:Decorate overrides the stand-down latch
findings.locations: modules/Canvas.lua:802, modules/Canvas.lua:823, modules/Unlock.lua:171-177, modules/Unlock.lua:123-126, settings/Schema.lua:503-509, settings/Slash.lua:342, settings/PanelEditor.lua:749-750
findings.evidence: Canvas:Render sets spec.shown=false when NS.Lifecycle:IsDown() (:802), then calls NS.Unlock:Decorate(f, rec) (:823). Decorate runs f:Show() and ArmDrag (EnableMouse, SetMovable, RegisterForDrag) and never consults the latch. A headless probe on the real TOC with two panels gave: unlocked then disabled, shown=2; disabled plus per-panel unlock, shown=1; disabled plus Lock frame unticked, shown=2; relocked, shown=0. Three routes reach it: (A) unlock then disable; (B) the Lock frame row or /pm set state.locked false while disabled; (C) the per-panel Unlock tick while disabled. Dragging a panel then writes db.profile.panels while the addon is off.
findings.remediation: In Canvas:Render, read the latch once (local down = NS.Lifecycle and NS.Lifecycle:IsDown()). If down, call NS.Unlock:StripOverlay(f); otherwise call NS.Unlock:Decorate(f, rec). Keep the session unlock state (NS.State.unlocked, unlockedPanels) untouched so NS.StandUp -> RenderAll restores the outlines from current state (performance-§6). Rejected alternatives: an imperative Hide or force-lock sweep in NS.StandDown (anti-pattern #85), and per-surface disabled gates. Land it test-first with R-02. Add an unlock-then-disable case to docs/smoke-tests.md.
findings.rule_ref: slash-commands-§7 (every frame hidden, enforced at the source); performance-§6; anti-pattern #85
findings.verify_reason: modules/Canvas.lua:802 sets spec.shown=false under NS.Lifecycle:IsDown(), then :823 calls NS.Unlock:Decorate unconditionally. modules/Unlock.lua:171-177 (Decorate) checks only IsPanelUnlocked, then runs f:Show() and ArmDrag (EnableMouse/SetMovable/RegisterForDrag). The latch is never consulted. NS.StandDown (core/LifecycleSetup.lua:93-95) only calls RenderAll, so an unlocked panel stays drawn and draggable. The schema Lock row (settings/Schema.lua:503-509) and the per-panel tick (PanelEditor.lua:749-750) reach SetUnlocked/SetPanelUnlocked without a disabled check. That breaks slash-commands-§7 ('The disabled state is total (MUST)'). Remediation is correct: branch on the latch in Render and call StripOverlay, keeping session state so StandUp -> RenderAll restores it. It adds no new deviation. Severity high holds because a MUST is broken on a common path, and drags write the DB while the addon is off.

findings.title: The stand-down conformance suite never unlocks a panel, so it stays green against R-01

Assert shownPanels() is empty and no panel frame has the mouse enabled. After re-enable, assert the unlocked panels come back decorated (the positive half). findings.title: 'Only in combat' and 'Only out of combat' visibility never flip at combat start because Compat.InCombat uses InCombatLockdown
findings.evidence: Compat.InCombat() returns InCombatLockdown(). Lockdown begins after PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED and ends before PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED, so it reads false inside both handlers. OnRegenDisabled -> RenderForCombat() therefore rebuilds every spec with inCombat=false. An inCombat profile stays hidden for the whole fight and an outOfCombat profile stays visible. events-frames-taint-§2 names this exact shape.
findings.remediation: Thread the transition's truth from the event: OnRegenDisabled -> NS.Canvas:RenderForCombat(true), and OnRegenEnabled -> RenderForCombat(false) after ResumePending. Add an optional inCombat parameter to Canvas:Render, RenderAll and RenderForCombat (Render defaults it to NS.Compat.InCombat()). Change Compat.InCombat() to prefer UnitAffectingCombat('player'), presence-guarded, with InCombatLockdown as the fallback. Add UnitAffectingCombat to .luacheckrc read_globals. Keep the unlock deferral on InCombatLockdown. Keep BuildSpec pure. Verify in-client (smoke C-03).
findings.verify_reason: core/Compat.lua:79-82 returns InCombatLockdown(). modules/Canvas.lua:787 feeds it to BuildSpec. core/PanelMaster.lua:116-127 has OnRegenDisabled -> RenderForCombat() -> RenderAll with no combat truth threaded through. At PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED lockdown has not begun, so the render uses inCombat=false and the 'inCombat'/'outOfCombat' modes do not flip at combat start. A caveat on the evidence: at REGEN_ENABLED the false reading is the CORRECT answer, so only the combat-start transition is broken. The stated impact (hidden or visible for the whole fight) is still accurate. events-frames-taint-§2 (STANDARDS.md v1.8.0 changelog, NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md:1267) says combat-reactive display SHOULD use UnitAffectingCombat and transitions SHOULD ride the REGEN events, which matches the finding. The remediation keeps the unlock deferral on InCombatLockdown, as the standard requires.

findings.title: /pm recover bounds scaled panel offsets against unscaled UIParent screen size
findings.locations: modules/Registry.lua:876-904, modules/Registry.lua:892-895, modules/Canvas.lua:566-569, modules/Canvas.lua:112-113, modules/Canvas.lua:85-89, modules/Unlock.lua:211
findings.evidence: applySpec calls SetScale(spec.scale) before SetPoint, so stored offsets are in the frame's scaled space (spec.scale = own scale x master Scale). R:Recover clamps rec.x/rec.y against Compat.GetScreenSize(), which is in UIParent units. At s=0.5 a visible TOPLEFT panel at x=3000 is moved; at s>1 a genuinely off-screen panel is left in place. The five existing Registry.Recover cases (tests/test_registry.lua:283-330) all run at scale 1.
findings.remediation: Add Util.EffectiveScale(rec, settings) in core/Util.lua (own scale clamped to MIN/MAX_PANEL_SCALE, times the master scale, default 1). Use it in Canvas addGeometry, which removes the now-unused masterScale. In R:Recover, bound with offsetRange(relPoint, w / s) and offsetRangeY(relPoint, h / s). Add two test_registry cases, red first: at scale 0.5, x=3000 is not moved; at scale 2, x=1500 is moved. Keep the five scale-1 cases unchanged.
findings.rule_ref: options-ui-§15 (master rows as multipliers; one definition shared by render and recover)
findings.verify_reason: The defect is real. applySpec (modules/Canvas.lua:566-569) calls SetScale(spec.scale) before SetPoint, so rec.x/rec.y are in the frame's scaled units. spec.scale = own scale x masterScale (Canvas.lua:85-89, 112-113). R:Recover (modules/Registry.lua:876-904) clamps against Compat.GetScreenSize() in UIParent units without dividing by scale. Severity lowered from high to medium: the impact is limited to an explicit, user-invoked /pm recover with a non-1 effective scale. It moves a visible panel, or fails to rescue an off-screen one, and the player can recover by dragging. No automatic path triggers it and nothing is lost beyond one position. The remediation is correct as written (bound with w/s and h/s, shared EffectiveScale helper, tests red first).

findings.title: A profile switch that swaps which id owns which frame name creates a duplicate named frame and orphans one each switch
findings.evidence: RenderAll resolves mismatches one id at a time. When id 1 wants a name still held by active[2], acquire runs CreateFrame with that global name a second time. When id 2 is released, its frame overwrites the pool slot, and the earlier frame becomes unreachable. A probe alternating {1 Alpha, 2 Xray}/{1 Xray, 2 Alpha} six times recorded 6 named CreateFrame calls, with PooledCount stuck at 1. test_profiles.lua never swaps ids.
findings.remediation: Make Canvas:RenderAll(inCombat) two-pass. First build want[id]=Registry.FrameName(rec), then release every active frame that is retired or whose __frameName is not want[id], then Render each id. Keep the Render(id) single-id mismatch branch as the fallback. Add a test_profiles case, red first, that swaps names across ids several times through OnProfileChanged and asserts zero named CreateFrame calls after the first render, plus _G-name/active identity.
findings.verify_reason: acquire (modules/Canvas.lua:36-40, pool keyed by global name) and the per-id mismatch branch in Render (:811-820), driven one id at a time by RenderAll (:829-842), show the problem. When id1 wants the name still held by active[id2], pool[name] is empty and newFrame creates a second frame with the same global name. A later release overwrites pool[name] and orphans a frame on each alternating switch. WoW frames are never collected, so this is a permanent leak, and _G[name] can point at a different frame than the active one. The pool's own comment (:25-40) claims the bound is one frame per name, which this breaks. The two-pass RenderAll remediation is sound and keeps the single-id fallback.

findings.title: The combat-visibility test raises the combat flag before delivering PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED, the reverse of the client's order

findings.title: The grid-size setting has two maxima: the slider stops at 64 while C.MAX_GRID allows 128
findings.evidence: The schema row declares max = 64, while its validate function and Unlock snap clamp use C.MAX_GRID = 128. The only way to reach a value between 65 and 128 is a hand-edited SavedVariables file.
findings.remediation: Use one constant. The recommended option is to lower C.MAX_GRID to 64, since no UI or CLI path could ever store more. The alternative is max = C.MAX_GRID. Add a test_schema case asserting S:FindRow('settings.gridSize').max == C.MAX_GRID.
findings.verify_reason: settings/Schema.lua:71-76 declares max=64, while its validate and modules/Unlock.lua:39 use C.MAX_GRID=128 (core/Constants.lua:100). The CLI clamps to row.max (libs/LibKa0s/Slash.lua:356), so /pm set cannot exceed 64. Only a hand-edited SV or a validate-only path such as an import can store 65-128. This is a real two-maxima drift with low impact. Either remediation option is fine.

findings.title: The per-panel Unlock tick on the Panels page can show a state the panel is not in
findings.evidence: The tick has no refresher. It reads IsPanelUnlocked, which is true whenever the global unlock is on, so unticking it while globally unlocked has no effect. A global lock clears per-panel unlocks without refreshing the editor. A combat-deferred unlock replayed on PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED leaves the box unticked.
findings.remediation: Give the tick a scalar refresher that reads NS.Unlock:IsPanelUnlocked(rec.id). Disable it, with a tooltip line, while the global unlock is on. From the end of U:SetUnlocked, U:SetPanelUnlocked and U:ResumePending, call NS.PanelEditor:RefreshUnlock() behind a presence guard (precedent: modules/Registry.lua:516). Do not add a new bus message. PanelEditor.lua is 1476 lines, so keep the change to 12 added lines or fewer, or land it after the issue #47 split; it must never cross 1500.
findings.verify_reason: settings/PanelEditor.lua:743-758 has no refresher (the comment says so). It reads IsPanelUnlocked, which returns true when NS.State.unlocked (modules/Unlock.lua:123-126), so unticking while globally unlocked does nothing visible. A global lock clears unlockedPanels without refreshing the editor. On deferral the box is forced unticked, and U:ResumePending (:271+) later unlocks the panel without refreshing it. The presence-guard precedent at modules/Registry.lua:516 is accurate. PanelEditor.lua is 1476 lines, so the layout-§1 MUST cap of 1500 (layout.md:57) makes the line-budget constraint correct. RefreshUnlock does not exist yet and must be added.

findings.title: Event registration has no per-event pcall and records rejected event names nowhere
findings.evidence: NS.StandUp registers three events with bare calls, and OnInitialize registers PLAYER_LOGIN bare. On retail an unknown name raises, so a throw would leave the later registrations, Canvas:Enable() and the repaint unbound, with nothing visible. This is two MUSTs. It is latent: no registered event is retired today.
findings.remediation: Add a file-local safeRegister(event, handler) in core/LifecycleSetup.lua that pcalls NS.addon:RegisterEvent, appends failures to NS.State.rejectedEvents and logs NS.Debug('Events', ...). Route all four registrations through it; StandDown keeps its bare UnregisterEvent. Surface 'rejected events: <n> (<names>)' in D:Diagnose() so /pm debug reaches it. C_EventUtils.IsEventValid is an optional SHOULD. Write the test first using the kit mock's M.__badEvents, with a red-under comment.
findings.verify_reason: core/LifecycleSetup.lua:126-129 makes three bare NS.addon:RegisterEvent calls, and core/PanelMaster.lua:63 registers PLAYER_LOGIN bare. There is no pcall and no rejected-event record anywhere in core/ (grep for pcall and rejected in LifecycleSetup and DebugLogSetup finds none). events-frames-taint.md:30-31 has both MUSTs: a pcall per event, and a rejected-name record the player can reach. D:Diagnose exists in core/DebugLogSetup.lua:82 to host the record. The kit mock supports M.__badEvents (tests/_kit/mock_base.lua:715-725). The risk is latent because every event registered today is valid, so low is right.

findings.title: The load-bearing TOC position of settings\Slash.lua (after Schema) has no comment
findings.evidence: Slash.lua builds its dispatcher at file scope from NS.SchemaRuntime members, which Schema.lua publishes, so Schema must load first. Only the OptionsSetup comment states the Schema ordering. The position became load-bearing with the Schema adoption (af8a935).
findings.remediation: Add a comment above PanelMaster.toc:97: '# Slash AFTER Schema, load-bearing: its dispatcher descriptor takes NS.SchemaRuntime's members as VALUES at file load (settings/Slash.lua:554-558).' tests/test_harness.lua already pins TOC order.
findings.verify_reason: PanelMaster.toc lists settings\Slash.lua right after settings\Schema.lua, with only the group header '# Settings (last ...)' above it. settings/Slash.lua:554-558 reads NS.SchemaRuntime.Get/Set/... at file load, and settings/Schema.lua:375 publishes NS.SchemaRuntime, so the position is load-bearing. toc-file.md:145 says a load-bearing line MUST carry a comment naming what resolves at load. A misorder would raise an index-nil error at load rather than fail silently, which supports low.

findings.title: The architecture-§5 register row's re-check trigger is met at the library layer (SchemaRuntime instance addressing) but has not been re-decided
findings.evidence: The trigger reads 'schema helper gains instance addressing'. S.Set(path, value, instanceId) now passes the id to resolveRoot, but the host resolver ignores it and the colon wrappers do not forward it. No open issue carries the owner's decision, and #49 is closed. The trigger text is ambiguous.
findings.remediation: Owner's decision, recorded either way. (a) Adopt: resolveRoot(parts, id) maps an id to the panel record, instance-relative rows are registered for C.PANEL_FIELD_TYPE fields, Registry:Set routes through NS.SchemaRuntime.Set(path, v, id), and the row retires. This is a large change and needs its own state:triaged issue. (b) Keep: re-word the trigger to the host-side condition, re-date the row, and file a state:triaged issue with option (a) as its body.
findings.rule_ref: audit-review-history (third MUST: evaluate every re-check trigger); architecture-§5
findings.verify_reason: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:378's re-check trigger is 'The schema helper gains instance addressing for registry records (an explicit record argument on NS.Schema:Set)'. libs/LibKa0s/Schema.lua:236 and :339-342 now thread instanceId through resolveRoot, and :432 gives S.Set(path, value, instanceId). The host resolver at settings/Schema.lua:360 ignores the id, and settings/Schema.lua:636 `S:Set(path, value)` does not forward one. The trigger is therefore arguably met at the library layer but not in the host wrapper. It is ambiguous, and audit-review-history requires every trigger to be evaluated. The fix is the owner's decision recorded in this repo's doc and issue, so no upstream routing is needed.

findings.title: The Lifecycle degradation stub has no surface-parity case, although a code comment and module-map.md say it does
findings.locations: core/LifecycleSetup.lua:147-190, tests/test_surface_parity.lua:3, tests/test_surface_parity.lua:59-226, docs/module-map.md:19, tests/run.lua (Kit.setSurfaceSource), tests/degraded_env.lua
findings.evidence: The stub has 9 members (Hold, Release, Set, IsHeld, IsDown, Holds, Reevaluate, PrintHolds, name). The parity suite has six cases (Core, DebugLog, Launcher, Slash, Options, Schema) and none for Lifecycle. Env and Media are not affected because they have no separate stub.
findings.remediation: Add 'Parity: the Lifecycle seam's degraded surface matches the live one'. Build the degraded arm with loadPartial or degraded_env omitting Lifecycle.lua, name the grep (grep -rn 'NS\.Lifecycle[:.]' core modules settings) in a comment, add ['LibKa0s-Lifecycle-1.0'] = NS.Lifecycle to Kit.setSurfaceSource, and put name in the ignore set if walked. Update the header count to seven and docs/testing.md:340-351.
findings.verify_reason: core/LifecycleSetup.lua:147-148 comment says tests/test_surface_parity.lua compares the two member sets, and docs/module-map.md:19 says the same. The stub at :150-185 has Hold/Release/Set/IsHeld/IsDown/Holds/Reevaluate/PrintHolds/name. test_surface_parity.lua has exactly six cases (lines 59, 103, 136, 154, 190, 226: Core, DebugLog, Launcher, Slash, Options, Schema) and the header at :3 says six. tests/run.lua:71-76 setSurfaceSource has no Lifecycle entry. The live side is an instance (Lifecycle:New at :196), so comparing stub against live instance (two-table form, as Core/Slash do) or mapping the major to NS.Lifecycle both work. Real drift gap, low severity.

findings.title: The kit prose gate scans frozen docs/superpowers/ and docs/investigations/; two frozen specs were respelled to the non-word 'catalogd'
findings.evidence: The kit's SKIPPED_DIRS (kit revision 25) omits docs/superpowers/ and docs/investigations/, which documentation-§3 lists as frozen. Commit e30e329 'fixed' line 5 of two frozen specs from 'catalogued' to 'catalogd'. The prior audit (PM-032a) had declined to touch these lines for this reason.
findings.remediation: Upstream first, in LibKa0s testkit/test_prose.lua: add 'docs/superpowers/' and 'docs/investigations/' to SKIPPED_DIRS, with a kit self-test pinning both the exclusion and its narrowness. Bump to kit revision 26, add a changelog entry, get the kit-sync gate green, and tag a patch. Then re-vendor the whole of LibKa0s and testkit. Then restore line 5 of both specs from 'git show e30e329^:<path>' and confirm test_prose stays green. Interim, if the re-vendor is delayed: skipDirs = { 'docs/superpowers/' } in tests/prose_waivers.lua, removed after the re-vendor.
findings.verify_reason: tests/_kit/test_prose.lua:209-213 SKIPPED_DIRS lists libs/, tests/_kit/, audits, automated-tests, perf-analysis, reviews and revendor, but not docs/superpowers/ or docs/investigations/. documentation.md:331-334 names both as frozen stores, and localization-§5 (localization.md:253-260) requires frozen material to be excluded, named directory by directory. `git show e30e329` confirms line 5 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-panel-artwork-design.md went from 'catalogued' to the non-word 'catalogd', and the 2026-08-02 spec's line 5 has the same text now. The file is vendored kit code, so the fix belongs upstream in LibKa0s testkit.

findings.title: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md has outgrown the hub shape: 471 lines, a 102-line Settings Schema section, retired-row narratives and non-canonical headings
findings.locations: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:30-131, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:47-78, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:80-103, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:132, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:288, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:380-428
findings.evidence:
- The file is 471 lines against a SHOULD of about 400.
- Settings Schema is 102 lines against the MUST to spill to schema.md at about 60.
- 49 lines of prose describe retired register rows.
- Two headings are not canonical: '## Message bus (architecture-§4)' should be 'Message Bus', and '## Taint' should be 'Taint Notes'.
findings.remediation: Move :47-78 (the schema-runtime adoption narrative, the stub and the Master controls composition) into docs/schema.md under '## The schema runtime'. Keep a summary of five lines or fewer, the registry naming (:80-103) and one link. Collapse the retired-row narratives to one line each, citing PM-029, #48 and the bundle. Rename the two headings and check tests/test_docs.lua for heading pins. Target: under 400 lines.
findings.verify_reason: `wc -l` gives 471 lines, against documentation.md:320's SHOULD of about 400. '## Settings Schema' runs from :30 to :131 (102 lines), past the ~60-line spill MUST at documentation.md:317-319, and docs/schema.md exists to receive it. The headings are '## Message bus (`architecture-§4`)' at :132 and '## Taint' at :288; documentation.md:127 names them 'Message Bus' and 'Taint Notes'. The long retired-row narratives are at about :380-428. tests/test_docs.lua has no heading pins for these. The audit rule itself says to report the shape rather than the arithmetic, so low is correct.

findings.title: docs/module-map.md misses 28 of 32 authored test files and 3 of 4 tools/ generators
findings.evidence: The basename check finds every test_*.lua except test_envsetup, test_harness, test_libka0s and test_surface_parity unmentioned, and the same for run.lua, wow_mock.lua, degraded_env.lua and prose_waivers.lua. Three artwork generators are also missing (03_EVIDENCE.md §10).
findings.remediation: Add a '## tests/' table: rows for run.lua, wow_mock.lua, degraded_env.lua and prose_waivers.lua, plus one row per suite or a suite-family table naming every file. Add a '## tools/' table with four generator rows describing what each writes.

Only test_envsetup, test_harness, test_libka0s and test_surface_parity appear. tools/artwork/artwork_cleaner.py, make_poster.py and update_catalog.py are also missing, while tools/sunn/build_manifest.py is present. documentation.md:235 requires module-map.md to cover every non-vendored file.

findings.title: Stale inventory counts and code comments in the docs and in PanelEditor.lua
findings.locations: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:21-24, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:339, docs/testing.md:106, docs/testing.md:340-351, docs/module-map.md:69-70, settings/PanelEditor.lua:178-190, settings/PanelEditor.lua:1191-1223, .gitignore:6
findings.evidence:
- ARCHITECTURE says 'six of eight seams'; there are nine.
- testing.md says 'nine of ten majors resolve Core'; it is fourteen of fifteen.
- testing.md says 'four seams adopted'; nine are adopted, with six parity cases (seven after A-08).
- module-map says 'other nine'; it should say fourteen.
- ARCHITECTURE:339 calls RESULTS.md 'never hand-edited', but its Disposition column is authored.
- PanelEditor comments say 'General is GONE', 'THREE EXPLICIT ROWS' and refreshHeaderActs, all of which are stale.
- .gitignore:6 cites a nonexistent tools/artwork/wiki_import.py.
findings.remediation: Do a single sweep, recounting with grep -c rather than by hand. Restate seven parity cases after A-08 lands. Rewrite the PanelEditor comment blocks: General is back and first, the band is one row, and refreshHeaderActs is gone. Keep the PanelEditor edit net-neutral given the 1500-line cap. Drop the wiki_import.py reference in .gitignore, or re-point it at the actual script.
findings.verify_reason:
Every claim checks out:
- ARCHITECTURE.md:20-21 says 'six of the eight LibKa0s seams'. 9 distinct LibKa0s majors are resolved in core/settings/modules, and 7 *Setup.lua files are in core alone.
- testing.md:106 says 'Nine of the ten majors'. The vendored lib names 15 majors.
- testing.md:340 says 'Four LibKa0s seams are adopted' (and 'Two of the four'); nine are adopted.
- module-map.md:69-70 says 'the other nine'.
- docs/automated-tests/RESULTS.md:5 says the Disposition column is authored, yet ARCHITECTURE.md:339 says 'never hand-edited'.
- settings/PanelEditor.lua:178 has 'General is GONE' but :192 says General is FIRST.
- PanelEditor.lua:1210 says 'THREE EXPLICIT ROWS' while :192 says the band is one row.
- refreshHeaderActs appears only in the comment at :1220.
- PanelEditor.lua is 1476 lines, so the net-neutral caution is apt.
- .gitignore:6 cites tools/artwork/wiki_import.py, which does not exist.

findings.title: README has angle-bracket placeholders that CurseForge strips, and Usage does not end on the configuration line
findings.evidence: /pm delete <name>, /pm get <setting> and /pm reset <setting> lose their argument on CurseForge. The configuration signpost sits mid-section and Usage ends on the disabled-state paragraph. Usage is nine paragraphs against guidance of five, which is not a breach.
findings.remediation: Write the arguments as bare examples (/pm delete ChatBG, /pm get settings.gridSize). Move the configuration pointer to Usage's last line. Merge the two disabled-state paragraphs. Run the /humanize de-AI pass.
findings.verify_reason: README.md:51 has `/pm delete <name>`, and :79-80 have `/pm get <setting>` and `/pm reset <setting>`. documentation.md:32-37 says angle-bracket placeholders MUST NOT appear in shipped README content, even inside backticks. In Usage, the configuration signpost ('Everything else is configuration...') is mid-section, and the section ends on the disabled-state paragraphs. The five-paragraph guidance at documentation.md:65 is explicitly 'not a breach'. The rendering impact is a lost argument on CurseForge, so low is correct.

findings.title: 25 vendored LibKa0s tags since 2026-08-25 have no re-vendor bundle naming them
findings.evidence: 32 commits touching libs/LibKa0s vendored 31 distinct tags, and bundles record 8. The 25 unrecorded tags run v1.18.0 through v1.53.0. The v1.55.0 bundle names only v1.54.2->v1.55.0.
findings.remediation: Write one consolidated bundle, docs/revendor/<date>-v1.16.0-to-v1.54.2/, with 01_DELTA.md and 05_SUMMARY.md. First line: '# 01 — Delta: LibKa0s v1.16.0 → v1.54.2 (consolidated)'. In the body, list every unrecorded vendored tag: v1.16.0, the 25 tags from v1.18.0 to v1.53.0, and v1.54.2. Also list the commits that carried them. Re-run AUDIT.md's two-listing check and confirm it prints nothing. If the check reads only the opening line's end tag, the enumerated list in the body must be the thing it reads. Do not write a folder per tag.
findings.rule_ref: audit-review-history (a re-vendor commit implies a bundle)
findings.verify_reason:
The defect is real (audit-review-history.md:34-58: every re-vendor commit after the store's first bundle needs a bundle naming its tag, and a consolidated bundle is allowed), but the span is wrong at both ends.
- The first bundle is 2f929fe (2026-08-25, v1.15.0), and bundles record v1.15, v1.25, v1.30-v1.34 and v1.55.
- Reading the provenance line at each libs/LibKa0s commit after the horizon gives 25 unrecorded tags from v1.18.0 to v1.53.0, as stated.
- It also gives v1.16.0 (eddcf3d, 2026-08-25 14:26, after the first bundle) and v1.54.2 (e30e329; the v1.55.0 bundle names it only as the source tag).
- Both extra tags are also unrecorded, so a v1.18.0-to-v1.53.0 bundle leaves the check still reporting gaps.

findings.title: AUDIT.md grades an unrecorded re-vendor tag High in its check text but Low in its step-5 table
findings.locations: WowAddonStandards AUDIT.md (re-vendor check vs step-5 grading table)
findings.evidence: This run graded PM-048 Low by step 5, and flagged the conflict for the documentation-lane audit of WowAddonStandards.
findings.remediation: File a proposal in the WowAddonStandards documentation lane to reconcile the re-vendor check's 'High' with step 5's Low grading for a missing record. This is a proposal only and does not block the addon.
findings.verify_reason: The conflict is real. WowAddonStandards/AUDIT.md:341-342 says 'A tag vendored with no bundle naming it and no ## Documented deviations row saying why is a **High** finding' (and :335 repeats 'High'). Step 5's grading table (AUDIT.md:~865-874) says a 'doc-only or config-only failure is Low or Info even when the rule it fails is a MUST', and High is kept for something a user, their SavedVariables or their session can hit today. A missing re-vendor record is doc-only. PanelMaster/docs/audits/2026-09-23/02_DEVIATIONS.md:348 files PM-048 as Low. The addon needs no change, so routing it to WowAddonStandards is correct.

findings.title: The standard has no ruling on migration-stamp ownership ('runner-stamped, never declared' for AceDB hosts)
findings.evidence: PanelMaster is a worked instance: a declared AceDB default masks legacy accounts (defaults/Global.lua:8-20, febf108). The MUST to declare schemaVersion in defaults conflicts with a correct migration for AceDB hosts.
findings.remediation: Propose a ruling in open-evolutions sanctioning 'stamped by the runner, never declared in defaults' for AceDB hosts, with PanelMaster as the worked case. If accepted, the A-05 register row becomes compliance and can retire.
findings.verify_reason: toc-file.md:55 (section 2) says 'MUST declare a schemaVersion integer in defaults', and savedvariables.md:10,18 (section 1) shows `global = { schemaVersion = 1 }` and says MUST declare it. PanelMaster/defaults/Global.lua:8-20 deliberately does not seed the stamp, and explains that the AceDB default masked legacy accounts. open-evolutions.md:15-24 already lists 'Migration-stamp ownership' as open and names this same AceDB backfill hard case, with no ruling yet. The finding is accurate. One nuance: the open-evolution entry already exists, so the action is to add PanelMaster as a worked case and push for a ruling, not to file a new entry.

findings.title: The automated-test record is 29 commits stale, and the 1.1.1 release has no release bundle
findings.evidence: The newest bundle, 20260916-184500 (sha 3c4005a, addon 1.1.0), recorded 834 tests, 1624 functions and 13887 NLOC; HEAD has 884, 1687 and 14325. No threshold was crossed and there is no watch-list drift. The 1.1.1 tag (1.1.1-release on dd04000) has no release bundle, and automated-tests-§5 forbids backfilling one.
findings.remediation: Cite automated-tests-§6 (a release MUST produce a four-suite bundle before the tag) for the 1.1.1 gap. Also cite automated-tests-§4 for the stale RESULTS trend. Close the gap forward: at the next release, run tests/_kit/run-automated-tests.sh through the ka0s-bounded runner as a release run via /wow-addon:bump-version. Carry the four band dispositions forward, and note once in that bundle's ANALYSIS.md that 1.1.1-release (dd04000) was tagged with no release bundle and with a TOC that still read 1.1.0. Do not create a bundle stamped for 1.1.1 after the fact.
findings.verify_reason: The facts check out. The newest bundle is 20260916-184500 (at 3c4005a), and `git rev-list --count 3c4005a..HEAD` returns 29. The 1.1.1-release tag is on dd04000, a 'Dummy commit to trigger a new build' whose TOC still reads 1.1.0. The TOC was only aligned to 1.1.1 afterwards, in 940bb11 on 2026-09-20. No bundle exists for that release. Three things needed correcting. (1) The rule is cited wrongly: automated-tests-§5's MUST NOT backfill (automated-tests.md:329) is about writing an ANALYSIS.md into an already-frozen bundle, not about creating a missing release bundle after the fact. The rule 1.1.1 actually missed is automated-tests-§6 (automated-tests.md:349: 'MUST produce a full four-suite bundle as part of every release … before the tag'). (2) Closing the gap forward is still the right call, because a bundle made at HEAD cannot measure dd04000. (3) A missed release MUST that is record-only grades Low under AUDIT step 5, not Info.

findings.locations: GitHub issues #19, #20, #22, #23, #24; CLAUDE.md:83; ADDONS.md:26; PanelMaster.toc:13; README.md:4; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:375
findings.evidence:
- #19: agent-context.md was deleted.
- #20: the addon is registered in ADDONS.md:26.
- #22: X-Curse-Project-ID 1642836 is present.
- #23: the CurseForge badge is present.
- #24: the performance-§1 row is ratified.
findings.remediation: Close #19, #20, #22 and #23 as state:done and #24 as state:will-not-do, each with a one-line evidence comment (gh issue close plus a label edit). Space out the API writes.
findings.rule_ref: audit-review-history (the issue store is the backlog)
findings.verify_reason: All five premises are resolved. #19 is about the respelled docs/agent-context.md, and that file no longer exists; CLAUDE.md:83 says it was deleted in v2.17.0 and must not be created. #20 asks for roster registration, and WowAddonStandards/standards/ADDONS.md:26 lists Ka0s Panel Master. #22 (D-001) is blocked on a CurseForge id, and PanelMaster.toc:13 now has X-Curse-Project-ID 1642836. #23 (D-002) is the missing curseforge badge, and README.md:4 now has it. #24 (no performance-§1 counterpart) is covered by docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:375, a row ratified by the owner on 2026-08-25. That was a deliberate decision not to wire the harness, so closing #24 as will-not-do is right. `gh issue list` confirms all five are open and labelled state:triaged.
